decisive_items: progressively worsening sharp epigastric pain radiating to the back
generalized abdominal tenderness worst in the epigastrium
response.rationale: Elevated lipase plus characteristic epigastric pain radiating to the back meet two of three criteria for acute pancreatitis; CT can be normal in early or mild disease. Other candidates do not explain the acute pain and marked lipase elevation.

rejected.why: Known CKD and elevated creatinine are chronic and do not explain acute epigastric pain or elevated lipase.
Pancreatic insufficiency is chronic and does not cause acute epigastric pain with elevated lipase; decreased intake and diabetes are nonspecific.
Hyperglycemia and diabetes are present, but there is no evidence of ketosis or acidosis, and glucose is only modestly elevated.
Epigastric pain and pantoprazole failure could suggest PUD, but PUD does not explain the markedly elevated lipase.
